name: Farm School
line: A learning lab on five acres. Day visits, short courses, internships and stays.
deck: Our own words for it are an organic, experiential, deconstructed un'education Learning Lab. In practice: five acres, an hour and a half from Delhi, and a farm that has to actually produce or the lesson is wrong.

figures.label: Dead leaves composted into soil on site

aims.h: Teach somewhere the lesson can be wrong
aims.p: Compost that fails and hives that empty are part of what a student sees here. No exhibit can offer that, which is the whole reason this is a farm and not a centre.

aims.h: One day should still leave a mark
aims.p: For the shortest visit the target is small and physical: something a person did themselves and can still describe a month later.

aims.h: Trust the long stays with something real
aims.p: An internship is meant to end with a person running part of this place unsupervised. If it ends in a certificate, it was a longer day visit.
Leaves into soil, flowers into honey, rain into groundwater. The aim is that the teaching material is what the place produces and what it throws away.

how.h: The classroom is a working farm
how.p: Permaculture and soil regeneration, water harvesting in swales, bundhs and ponds, solar, an apiary, a dairy prototype. None of it is a demonstration model. If it stops producing, the lesson stops being true.
Close enough to reach on a school morning. Far enough that by lunch the city has stopped being the thing everything is measured against.

activities.name: A day visit
activities.p: A bus and a packed lunch. One thing done with your hands, ninety minutes out, and back by evening. It is the widest door and the one most people come through.

frame.alt: A bamboo and netting frame over a cultivated plot

activities.name: Short courses, and the five C's
activities.p: Connection, creativity, confidence, cognition, cycle. That is the course frame, and it is deliberately not a syllabus: the farm sets the week and the week sets the lesson.

frame.alt: Trays of microgreens under grow racks

activities.name: Internships and stays
activities.p: The stay is weeks rather than hours, and the difference shows up in what a person is trusted to do by the end of it.

frame.alt: Turmeric plants at knee height, two figures working the rows behind

who.h: School groups on a day out
who.p: A bus, a morning and a working farm. The day visit is the widest door and the shortest commitment on the whole register.
Teachers and facilitators come for the short courses, which is the part of this that travels back into a classroom we never see.
People who want weeks rather than hours and are willing to be given a job. What they are trusted with by the end is the measure of it.

who.h: Rooms of adults who need the city to stop being the reference point
who.p: Team meetings and retreats happen here too. The farm does not distinguish much between a school group and a board, and neither do the chores.

done.h: Five thousand kilos of leaves, turned into soil
done.p: Around 5,000 kg of dead leaves composted on site — the farm's own waste stream, closed on the farm.
From the apiary, which is also the part of the farm that teaches the most about what a monoculture costs, without anybody having to say the word.

holes.what: Nobody is named as a partner or a funder here.
holes.unlocks: A supporter list would let this page do what Bridge the Gap's does — name who paid for the unglamorous middle.

statement.line: A farm that stops producing stops teaching.
statement.under: The apiary, the compost and the water works are not exhibits. They are the syllabus, and they are allowed to fail.
